paper_metadata.title: Applying Quantum Computing to the Renewable Energy Stock Exchange to Reduce the Risk of Investment
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of World Conference on Information Systems for Business Management (ISBM 2023), Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems, Vol. 833, Springer

summary: Chapter applies Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) simulation to estimate survival functions for daily (2020-2023) returns of eight major renewable-energy stocks (IBDRY, NEE, VWDRY, JKS, CSIQ, DQ, AQN, CWEN; 837 daily obs each). The authors frame HMC as a 'quantum-computing-inspired' technique but implement it as a classical Bayesian MCMC sampler and derive per-stock survival probabilities and recommended holding horizons. Reported holding horizons: IBDRY 10 mo @ 84.6%, NEE 11 mo @ 85.7%, VWDRY 6 mo @ 74.5%, JKS 5 mo @ 89.3%, CSIQ 12 mo @ 85.7%, DQ 6 mo @ 82.1%, AQN 5 mo @ 81.8%, CWEN 12 mo @ 81.5%. No quantum hardware or simulator used; no gate-based quantum algorithm implemented.

experiments.description: HMC-based survival-function estimation for eight renewable-energy stocks. Daily prices Jan 2020 - 2023 (approx. 837 obs per stock) for IBDRY, NEE, VWDRY, JKS, CSIQ, DQ, AQN, CWEN. Descriptive statistics (mean, median, min/max, skewness, kurtosis, Jarque-Bera, PP unit-root) computed for both adjusted-close and open-price return series (Tables 2-3). HMC Markov-chain Monte Carlo sampler used to sample from posterior survival-time distribution; per-stock survival probability and corresponding holding horizon reported.

algorithm.variant: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) MCMC sampler for Bayesian survival-function estimation; framed by authors as quantum-inspired but implemented as classical Hamiltonian dynamics + Metropolis acceptance
algorithm.optimizer: HMC sampling (Hamiltonian dynamics with leapfrog integrator + MH accept/reject)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Daily price returns per stock used as observations; Bayesian posterior over survival times sampled via HMC; survival function S(t) = P(T > t) estimated from posterior samples.
problem_formulation.constraints: Returns required to be stationary (confirmed via PP unit-root test, p=0.000); no additional operational constraints.

problem_instance.dataset_name: Daily OHLC prices for eight renewable-energy stocks (Yahoo Finance), 2020-2023

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: Renewable-energy equities: IBDRY, NEE, VWDRY, JKS, CSIQ, DQ, AQN, CWEN
dataset_specification.description: Daily adjusted-close and open prices; 837 daily observations per stock after cleaning; return series tested for stationarity (PP unit-root, Jarque-Bera).

results.notes: DQ (Daqo New Energy) at 6-month horizon (Section 4.2, Fig. 10).

speedup_claims.notes: No speedup demonstrated. Paper asserts quantum computing 'potential' for finance in narrative framing but does not benchmark against any classical or quantum alternative.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: HMC sampling: per-iteration cost O(L * d) where L is leapfrog steps and d is parameter dimension; number of iterations and chains not reported.

notes: All survival probabilities and horizons read from Section 4.2 (pp. 467-473). Descriptive-statistics panel (Tables 2-3) confirms 837 daily observations per stock and stationarity (PP p=0.000), non-normal returns (Jarque-Bera p=0.000).
HMC is a classical MCMC technique; the paper's 'quantum' framing is rhetorical. No quantum hardware, simulator, circuit, or qubit count is reported.
Extraction classifies the work as quantum-inspired classical simulation within the quantitative pipeline, per the quantitative-silo audit rule for HMC/quantum-inspired methods.
